title: Cell Cycle Control of Arterial-Venous Specification
text:
We are studying the process of blood vessel formation and trying to understand how the growth of endothelial
cells, that form the lining of blood vessels, is regulated and to what extent this is necessary in order to develop
a proper blood circulatory system. By defining factors that are needed for endothelial cell growth control and
arterial-venous network development, we will gain insights needed to treat arterial-venous malformations,
enhance neovascularization of injured tissues, and engineer circulatory networks from human stem cells that
can be used for tissue engineering and regenerative medicine applications.

title: Understanding the Genetic Contributions to Variation in Ozone Exposure Response
text:
Ozone is a common ambient air pollutant that causes pulmonary inflammation and decreased lung function upon
acute exposure and is further associated with chronic respiratory diseases including asthma and COPD. There
is ample evidence of interindividual variation in response to ozone in humans, but the genetic contribution to this
variation is largely unknown. This study will use an in vitro model of the human lung featuring genetic diversity
to identify risk variants for severe response to acute ozone exposure, then assess their overlap with asthma and
COPD risk variants, which will guide identification of high-risk individuals.

title: The crosstalk of organelles involved in autophagosome biogenesis
text:
The crosstalk of organelles including fusion and contact is involved in different stages of autophagy.
SNAREs, vacuolar protein sorting-associated protein 33A, and Atg9 play a critical role in regulating
the crosstalk of organelles, which is essential for autophagosome biogenesis.

title: Cell-Free DNA Methylation Patterns as a Biomarker for Tumor Biology and Clinical Outcomes for Glioblastoma Patients
text:
Glioblastoma is the most common primary malignant brain tumor in adults and remains fatal despite aggressive
treatments. One of the main barriers to understanding glioblastoma tumor biology and developing more effective
therapies is the dependence on tumor tissue obtained via invasive surgical procedures for diagnosis. This work
will evaluate whether cell-free DNA methylation patterns derived from peripheral blood correlate with tumor
biology and treatment response, thereby providing a method for longitudinal molecular profiling.

title: Defining the Role of Epidermal NADPH in Linking Skin Homeostasis to Systemic Metabolism.
text:
The skin is more than a protective barrier—it is an active organ that communicates
with the rest of the body. This study will determine how a molecule called NADPH helps the skin defend itself
against oxidative damage and maintain its barrier, and how the loss of NADPH can send signals from the skin
that lead to fat loss throughout the body. Understanding this “skin-to-body” communication may lead to new
treatments for skin conditions such as eczema and advance our understanding of how skin metabolism
influences whole-body metabolic health.

title: Next Generation Cone Beam CT with Improved Contrast Resolution and Added Spectral Imaging Functionality
text:
Cone beam CT (CBCT) is becoming an indispensable imaging modality for minimally invasive image-guided
interventions. High quality CBCT imaging plays a pivotal role in guaranteeing the success of diagnostic and
treatment procedures. In this project, a new CBCT imaging platform that integrates both a photon counting
detector and a flat panel detector to provide much improved soft-tissue contrast detectability and quantitative
spectral CT image guidance will be developed to enable more accurate diagnoses and image guidance for
treatment planning and treatment delivery.

title: The Circuit Logic of Modulation of Locomotion by Odors
text:
Public health: The ability to execute complex behaviors in response to sensory responses is disrupted in
many diseases. The research proposed here is aimed at understanding the logic underlying the control of
complex behavior and how this control is organized in neural circuits. This understanding will lead to better
management of diseases affecting proper execution of behavior.

title: Mechanisms of Kidney Diseases Associated With APOL1 Variation
text: Chronic kidney diseases (CKD) are common, costly and a significant burden on patients and their families. Genetic variants in the APOL1 gene explain part of the excess CKD risk. This project will define the pathways that translate the genetic association into disease and could identify novel targets for effective CKD treatments in this high-risk population.

title: Effects of vaping-induced oxidation on nicotine analogs e-cigarettes
text:
The vaping landscape has significantly evolved, with rising popularity among adolescents and young adults,
driven by various flavorings and addictive substances, including different forms of nicotine. Despite regulatory
efforts, youth vaping persists, particularly with the increase in disposable devices and the emergence of
alternative nicotine formulations like 6-methyl nicotine, which presents higher toxicity and safety concerns. This
project aims to evaluate the chemical composition and toxicity of 6-methyl nicotine and nicotinamide vapes,
utilizing advanced mass spectrometry and in vitro exposure systems to inform regulatory decision-making and
further research on the health impacts of these vaping products.

title: Development of integrated OCT/US/PAT system for intravascular Imaging
text:
Coronary artery disease (CAD) is the most common type of heart-related issue, affecting over 18 million
adults and resulting in more than 350,000 deaths annually in recent years. Our objective is to develop an
advanced intravascular imaging system that combines the high spatial resolution of optical coherence
tomography, the broad imaging depth of ultrasound, and the high molecular sensitivity of photoacoustic
tomography. This system will assist doctors in detecting high-risk areas, customizing treatments, and monitoring
the progression of the disease and therapeutic effectiveness. It will serve as a potent tool, offering a quantitative
means to benchmark and evaluate new medical devices and therapies.

title: Multimodal imaging of prenatal alcohol exposure: Mechanisms underlying spatial navigation memory deficits in children and adolescents
text:
This project will identify neural circuitry and brain dynamics involved in spatial memory deficits during virtual
navigation in children with prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) and typically developing children and adolescents.
Determining the neural mechanisms underlying spatial navigation memory deficits in children with PAE will
provide foundational knowledge on how PAE alters brain function and a novel scientific framework allowing for
the identification of potential treatments and interventions.

title: Unravelling the Neural Basis of Bimanual Coordination in Mouse Motor Cortex
text:
Current treatments for Parkinson’s Disease (PD) struggle to restore patients’ abilities to coordinate movement
of both hands. In this project, I will study how the brain normally organizes its activity to enable bimanual
coordination and ask how this organization breaks down in a mouse model for PD. I aim to provide a new
target for future PD treatment strategies that address deficits to bimanual coordination by shifting patterns of
neural activity toward a healthy state.

title: Integrating machine learning to improve kidney disease risk assessment for patients on cancer therapy
text:
Currently, clinicians caring for patients with cancer and other malignancies lack a framework to generate
personalized risk assessments for adverse kidney outcomes and little is known about the long-term kidney
effects of many first-line molecularly-targeted therapies for breast, lung, and other cancers that often cause an
acute increase in serum creatinine once started. These oral medications are continued daily for months to
years and the risk factors and mechanism behind the acute and progressive changes in kidney function on
these medications is poorly understood. This project proposes to identify the incidence and risk factors of
progressive chronic kidney disease for patients on these molecularly targeted cancer therapies associated with
an acute increase in serum creatinine, determine change in kidney biomarkers of tubular injury at drug start,
and develop a personalized assessment tool harnessing rich electronic health data using machine learning
techniques to classify a patient on molecularly targeted cancer therapies’ risk for progressive chronic kidney
disease.

title: Identification of epigenetic etiologies for rare undiagnosed disorders
text:
Rare genetic diseases often remain undiagnosed despite extensive clinical and genomic testing, leading to
significant healthcare impact worldwide. This supplemental proposal will incorporate epigenomic studies into
the Undiagnosed Diseases Network diagnostic workflow to identify known and novel methylation-related
disorders in families who remain unsolved after comprehensive genomic evaluation. By expanding diagnostic
approaches to include epigenetic disorders, these studies aim to reduce the diagnostic gap and improve care
for patients and families with undiagnosed rare diseases.

title: Innovating Measurement of Youth Social Media Activity: An Approach for Using a Large Language-Based Computer Vision Model to Study What Youth Are Doing on Social Media and Links to Mental Health
text:
This project has the potential to develop an artificial intelligence computer vision methodology that can be used
to advance an objective, ecologically valid measurement of youth social media (SM) use as it naturally occurs
in daily life and can be used in large-scale research. This project lays the foundation for future research de-
signed to rigorously investigate bidirectional associations between SM use and mental health in youth. Find-
ings from this area of research will help to inform (1) identification of aspects of SM use that may increase or
protect against risk for mental health problems among youth, (2) aspects of SM that may serve as targets for
mental health interventions, and (3) practice and policy recommendations for youth SM use in adolescence.

title: Functional genomics of GxE in cardiovascular disease: BPA, phthalates and their interactions with gene regulation
text:
Cardiovascular disease accounts for nearly 1 of every 3 deaths in the US, an average of 1 death every 38
seconds. The purpose of this project is to use functional genomic assays and novel statistical and computa-
tional methods to identify common genetic factors that interact with BPA and phthalates exposure and provide a
molecular mechanism for inter-individual variation in endothelial function and cardiovascular health.

title: Efficient, cost-effective, and ultrasensitive sequencing of somatic mutations and methylation
text:
Next-Generation DNA sequencing is now widely used in clinical oncology to detect mutations in
cancers that inform prognosis and therapeutic options, but is limited in its sensitivity for low-prevalence
variants. This proposal outlines the development and validation of inexpensive, efficient, and ultrasensitive
methods for detecting cancer-relevant mutations and methylation patterns in clinical specimens. This
technology will be immediately translatable and practical for clinical diagnostics, and will provide enhanced
capabilities in a broad range of applications, including the identification of emerging cancer subclones and
ultrasensitive screening for the emergence or recurrence of malignancy.

title: Mentored Vision Clinician-Scientist Program at OHSU
text:
Americans fear blindness more than virtually any other health problem, and the enormous impact of these
conditions will accelerate as our population ages. Fortunately, advances in scientific knowledge and technology
hold great promise for alleviating these problems. This proposal provides protected, start-up support for junior
faculty clinicians to develop the clinical research skills necessary to make this promise a reality and reduce the
suffering and impairment of blinding eye diseases.

title: Imaging the effects of transcranial alternatingcurrent stimulation in an experimental model of Alzheimer's Disease
text:
Despite the availability and promise of transcranial alternating current stimulation, its
effectiveness at arresting memory decline has hitherto been limited and highly variable across
Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) patients. Our experimental AD model studies will leverage novel
approaches to cellular-level interrogation of neuronal function and relate the cellular scale
changes in brain activity elicited by tACS to mesoscopic scale changes in neurotransmitter levels
and flux, and working memory. We will establish multi-scale machine learning models for
predicting the effects of transcranial alternating current stimulation on neuronal activity and
working memory using clinic-ready neuroimaging protocols, so as to lay the foundation for
development of personalized neuromodulation interventions for treating memory deficits in the
early stage of AD pathology.

title: The role of ganglioside GD3 in Alcohol-associated Liver Disease (ALD)
text: Nutrition and gut microbiota are associated with the development of ALD. Gut sialylation is a key force in maintaining a homeostatic relationship between the gut and its microbiota. Gangliosides are complex glycosphingolipids that contain a ceramide and an oligosaccharide fragment, and synthesized from lactosylceramide by sequential activities of sialyltransferases including ST8SIA1. ST8SIA1 catalyzes the transfer of sialic acid from CMP-sialic acid to ganglioside GM3 to produce GD3. It is unclear whether ganglioside GD3 regulate ALD. Ceramide is hydrolyzed to generate sphingosine and fatty acid by ceramidases including neutral ceramidase (NcDase). deletion of expression of ST8SIA1 and changes the levels We found that NcDase in intestinal epithelial cell (IEC) increases the of microbial metabolites in mice. We also showed that ST8SIA1/GD3 are associated with microbial metabolites and the development of ALD in mice. We identified that ganglioside GD3 is a functional ligand for Siglec-E on macrophages and promotes the polarization of macrophage via binding of Siglec-E. This has led to the central hypothesis that IECs NcDase regulates the intestinal sialylation and subsequent GD3 production via microbial metabolites; and that IEC GD3 regulates the plasticity of hepatic macrophage via GD3-Siglec-E signal and prevents the development of ALD. Importantly, the proposal also pursues translational studies that examine the efficacy of microbial metabolite and prebiotics GD3 treatment targeted at intestinal sialylation and hepatic inflammatory macrophages in mitigating gut-liver axis changes. Following specific aims will be carried out: Aim 1 will determine the impact of ST8SIA1 on the gut sialylation and the effects of this impact on intestinal barrier integrity in ALD. We will apply multi-omics approaches to identify sialylated glycosphingolipids and glycoproteins related to intestine integrity and macrophage plasticity in ALD. We will screen microbiota and its metabolites that can activate and correlate with ST8SIA1 expression and GD3 production. Aim 2 will determine if microbial metabolite mediated-HIF-1α activation regulates the activity of ST8SIA1 in vivo and in vitro. Aim 3 will evaluate the efficacy of ganglioside GD3 treatment-based immunotherapy in ALD and define the mechanism by which GD3 impacts hepatic macrophage plasticity via CyTOF, spatial distribution-IMCs and scRNA-seq. The successful completion of this project will likely bring new mechanistic understanding and identify new therapeutic targets for the prevention and treatment of ALD.
